evidence: When customers search in our store for something to buy, we show them products we think they’ll be most satisfied with.

evidence: based on factors like customer actions (such as how frequently an item was purchased by other customers)

claim: Amazon names the product's price, delivery speed, and what is hot and new as factors.
evidence: the product’s price, delivery speed, what’s hot and new

claim: Amazon names measures of post-purchase satisfaction, such as return rates, as a factor.
evidence: measures of post-purchase satisfaction like return rates

claim: When customers are dissatisfied, Amazon ranks products customers are more likely to love higher in search results.
evidence: we rank other products—ones we’ve determined customers are more likely to love—higher in search results.

claim: Amazon Australia says its search predictions use information about the item, such as the title, price and description.

claim: Amazon says its systems now better understand the intent behind a customer's search.
evidence: Our systems now better understand the intent behind a customer's search.

claim: Amazon says search is no longer just about matching keywords but about understanding what customers want to buy.
evidence: It's not just about matching keywords anymore—it's understanding what customers are actually looking to buy.

claim: Amazon says the Featured Offer is chosen on criteria such as low price including delivery and fast delivery, and customer preference determines it.
evidence: Customer preference determines which offer we feature.

claim: A DISCOVERABLE item is one customers can find in search results, whether or not it is on sale.
evidence: Items that customers can find in the search results but are not necessarily on sale.

claim: When a listing is search suppressed, it is no longer discoverable.
evidence: For example, when a listing is search suppressed, it is no longer discoverable.

claim: Listing issues cause listings to go inactive, search suppression, or other quality problems.
evidence: Issues point out that the listings item has problems which cause listings to go inactive, search suppression, or other quality problems.

claim: The generic_keyword (search terms) attribute has a documented maximum of 500 bytes.
evidence: generic_keyword: 500 bytes

claim: Item Highlights are fully searchable.
evidence: They are fully searchable, so customers can discover your product through the details you include in this field.

claim: The Search Query Performance dashboard lists the keywords customers use to find a brand.
evidence: lists keywords customers use to find your brand

claim: Brand Analytics requires a Professional selling account and a Brand Representative role for a brand enrolled in Brand Registry.
evidence: To access Brand Analytics, you need a Professional selling account.

claim: Brand Analytics lets brands monitor impressions, clicks, cart adds and purchases.
evidence: Monitor impressions, clicks, cart adds, and purchases.

claim: Search Catalog Performance helps identify drop-off points in product discoverability and sales conversion.
evidence: Identify drop-off points and address problems with product discoverability and sales conversion.

claim: A+ Content is free for sellers who meet the eligibility requirements.
evidence: A+ Content is free for sellers who meet eligibility requirements.

claim: Amazon says Basic A+ Content can increase sales by up to 8% and well-implemented Premium A+ Content by up to 20%, citing internal data.
evidence: Basic A+ Content can increase sales by up to 8%—and well-implemented Premium A+ Content can increase sales by up to 20%.

claim: Keywords can be used in product titles, descriptions, bullet points and more.
evidence: You can use keywords in your product titles, descriptions, bullet points, and more.

claim: Adding high-ranking search terms or keywords can help customers find a listing through search results.
evidence: Adding high-ranking search terms or keywords can help customers find your Amazon product listing through search results.

claim: Amazon advises keyword research and weaving critical words and phrases into product listing copy.
evidence: Do keyword research and weave critical words and phrases into your copy for webpages, product listings

evidence: your ads may be displayed at the top of, alongside, or within shopping results and on product pages.

claim: Products must be eligible for the Featured Offer to be advertised with Sponsored Products.
evidence: Products must be in one or more eligible categories and be eligible for the Featured Offer in order to advertise.

claim: Through the Selling Partner API, the Search Query Performance and Search Catalog Performance reports can be requested by sellers who have the Brand Analytics role and are registered in Amazon Brand Registry; the Amazon Search Terms report also requires being a brand representative.
evidence: Sellers who have the Brand Analytics Selling Partner API role and are registered in Amazon Brand Registry

claim: The Search Query Performance report gives impressions, clicks, cart adds and purchases for specified ASINs, at WEEK, MONTH or QUARTER periods, and requests cannot span multiple periods.
evidence: Data is available at different reporting periods: WEEK, MONTH, and QUARTER. Requests cannot span multiple periods.

claim: The Search Catalog Performance report provides search engagement metrics such as impressions, clicks, cart adds and purchases.
evidence: The Search Catalog Performance report provides search engagement metrics, such as impressions, clicks, cart adds, and purchases for a date range that you specify.
verifier_note: verifier-V5-3: table cell reworded to 'Search engagement metrics (impressions, clicks, cart adds, purchases) by ASIN'; 'across all queries' was not in this claim.

claim: The Search Terms report shares data on the top three clicked ASINs by search keyword and department for a marketplace; its fields include searchFrequencyRank, clickShare and conversionShare.
evidence: The Search Terms report shares data on the top-3 clicked ASINs by search keyword and department for a marketplace.

claim: searchQueryVolume is the number of times customers search for a query in the selected period.
evidence: The number of times customers search for a query at a select time period.

claim: asinImpressionShare is the fraction of impressions for the ASIN compared with the total impression count for the query.
evidence: The fraction of impressions for the ASIN in comparison to the total impression count for the query.

claim: asinClickShare, asinCartAddShare and asinPurchaseShare are the ASIN's fractions of the query's total clicks, cart adds and purchases.
evidence: The fraction of clicks for the current ASIN in comparison to the total click count for the query.

claim: searchQueryScore ranks a search query against the ASIN's other queries on overall performance, with 1 as the highest rank.
evidence: The rank for a search query in comparison to other queries for the ASIN. The ranking mechanism measures overall performance (the highest rank is 1).

claim: In Search Catalog Performance, clickRate is the number of clicks divided by the number of impressions for the ASIN.
evidence: The number of clicks divided by the number of impressions for the ASIN.

claim: In Search Catalog Performance, conversionRate is the number of purchases divided by the number of clicks for the ASIN.
evidence: The number of purchases divided by the number of clicks for the ASIN.

claim: Search Catalog Performance impressions count every time the ASIN displays on the search results page and include sponsored search results.
evidence: Amazon counts an impression every time the ASIN displays in the search results page. Impressions include sponsored search results.
verifier_note: verifier-V5-3: claim is about Search Catalog Performance; the summary bullet that attributed it to Search Query Performance was corrected, and 'an ad campaign can raise impression counts without any change in organic placement' was cut back to 'the count is not an organic-only measure'.

claim: The ASIN list in a Search Query Performance request is space-separated and has a 200-character limit.
evidence: A space-separated list of ASINs for which you can request the report. There is a 200-character limit.

claim: The search reports count clicks, cart adds and purchases separately for ASINs shown with same-day, one-day and two-day delivery messages.
evidence: The number of times customers click on the ASIN with the same day delivery message on the search results page.
